conclusions: The pressure campaign admits all seven honest submissions, but independent page replay 2 reaches PUBLIC_REQUEST_DEADLINE during native work at 4.000600734 seconds; only page 1 was accepted, so final transaction confirmation never ran.

The server mutation CPU meter never refuses and finishes near its original 2-second burst. The verifier first page separately waits about 493 ms for cold local CPU admission; these are distinct budgets.

The first successful pressure work has 1099 fresh Host checkpoint calls; the failed second work stops after 704. No missing or rejected Host check is reported. Host CPU sums invoking threads, while native phase CPU is the importer thread; do not sum or interpret their ratio as a full-process CPU allocation.

Existing paid FIFO/backpressure is active (315 enqueued after backpressure, 4384 retry events), and the rejection cache is active (328 cached refusals, 54 native false replays). Enabling either is not an unimplemented fix.

The fixed parent is verified at 25000/100000 CPU with zero burst. Whole-campaign kernel counters show throttling, and native work wall substantially exceeds caller CPU; these support CPU-contention as a hypothesis but do not allocate every 4-second wait to a kernel scheduling cause.

The 361406707 ns attack-worker scope includes 283358488 ns within calls plus 78048219 ns outside those call spans. The latter includes the existing fixture preparation/diagnostic path and is not removable under the unchanged benchmark constraint.

overlap_demonstrated=false is conditional on absent confirmation; there were still 377 completed false refusals after business start and before the 4-second end. full_native_state_equal=false is expected from incomplete independent replay and is not evidence of invalid-state acceptance.

The dependency-bound encoding helper uses exactly the same 16 false payloads and unchanged lock as f34, but it remains a component experiment. Faster calls can increase negative-call throughput; no fixed-count saving establishes confirmation success.
